newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed underpinned by firmer Chicago.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed underpinned by firmer Chicago.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in northwest Europe took support from a firmer Chicago market and tight domestic supplies, brokers said.
But trade remained very thin because crushers were achieving very low margins at current prices and so were turning to sunseed or soybeans.
November trade buyers free Hamburg were up five marks on the week at 455 for Nov/Dec, but sellers were seven marks higher.
Brokers said the market might have found a floor and further gains could come from lower U.S. crop estimates and dollar movements next week.
Reductions in the Canadian canola crop figure and rapeseed demand from Scandinavia also supported the market.
Rapeseed buyers at points other than Hamburg offered 445-467 marks for November.
French December seed FOB Moselle traded at 1,490 francs a tonne and January buyers offered 1,510.

Oelmuehle Hamburg AG (Oelag) this week received its first U.S. new crop soybean supply and said it was expecting a steady flow of shipments in the coming months, which would reduce its need to process rapeseed.
Oelag said it would shrug off protests from environmental groups campaigning against the use of genetically modified U.S. soybeans.
Nov/Jan rape oil was unquoted in Rotterdam but Feb/April oil had a 4.50 guilders premium over soyoil for that period at 95.50 guilders per 100 kilos fob mill.
Brokers said this reduced EU sales opportunities to China, where the U.S. has sold large volumes of soyoil this week.
Local rape meal sellers (34 percent protein) were broadly steady compared with last week at 30.00-30.25 marks/100 kg (Nov), with Dec at 29.50 and Jan/April at 28.75.
Local Nov/Jan rape oil sellers were at 83.75 marks/100 kg, up 2.25 on the week, and Feb/April oil was at 85.00, up 1.50.
